title: Working with Lee Collins in LaSalle, Illinois, and the Moulin Rouge
summary: Gabriel recalls leaving the Moulin Rouge in New Orleans to join Lee Collins in LaSalle, living in tiny Spring Valley because no Black residents lived nearby.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: They were talking about you and the pay. Yes, that's when I left and went to Florida. But some of the interesting things that I run into before that, which was, I went to work with Lee Collins. I don't know how he found out about me. Somebody told him about me when I was in New Orleans. I was working at the Moulin Rouge then.
Okay, now that was in the French Quarter.
Could you tell me where Moulin Rouge was?
On Burgundy and Bienville Street. That was owned by Elmo Badon. Elmo Badon, that's Pete Herman's brother-in-law.

Pete Herman was my sister and they were clubs were one block apart. So Lee Collins heard about me and sent for me to go to work with them in LaSalle, Illinois, as a teeniest silver Congo. We followed Ethel Waters in there. Now, the funny thing about that, we worked in LaSalle, but we had to live three cities away. Spring Valley we lived in. There was a town in between they called Piru, Illinois. There were no blacks living in those Piru, no LaSalle. And in Spring Valley, there was a total of 23 blacks living in there. And that included the three of us with Lee Collins and I brought a piano player with me. I hope his name would come to me. Walt.
